variants.name: Vapor Leaf templates (#(var), #extend/#embed)
variants.implementation_notes: Server-side Swift renders through Leaf in Vapor: configure app.views.use(.leaf), keep .leaf templates under Resources/Views and call req.view.render("orders", ["title": "Orders", "rows": rows]), which returns the View used as the response body. Markers are #(name) with #for/#if tags and #extend/#embed for layout; rendering goes through the generic req.view property, which keeps the renderer swappable in tests, and Leaf caches compiled templates outside development.
pitfalls: The views folder is a runtime resource: with Xcode you must set the working directory, or Leaf reports a missing template that exists on disk.
Leaf escapes #(...) by default but raw-printing tags do not; audit them like any unescaped marker.
In production the template cache is enabled, so an edited .leaf file is not picked up until the application restarts.

variants.name: Stencil engine (Django/Mustache-like, framework-independent)
variants.implementation_notes: Stencil is the engine-independent option: {{ value }} and {% for %}/{% if %}/{% include %}/{% extends %} tags over a [String: Any] context, rendered by Environment(loader: FileSystemLoader(paths: ["templates"])). It follows the Django philosophy - templates express presentation, not program logic - and is used by code generators and non-Vapor servers as well as by Stencil's listed adopters (Sourcery, SwiftGen). Choose it when the app is not Vapor or when templates must stay logic-light.
variants.idiom_name: Stencil Environment + FileSystemLoader over a [String: Any] context
pitfalls: The context is a plain [String: Any]: a wrong key or type renders as empty or throws at render time, so keep a render test per template.
Templates are loaded from a filesystem path at runtime, so the template directory must be shipped and the working directory known in every environment.
Errors are thrown while rendering and point into the template; wrap rendering so a template bug becomes a 500 rather than a crash.
